subject: Failover & SLO fallback: customer communication and next steps
messages:

Cc: ops@zenyard.io

Subject: Observed SLO fallback + partial responses — urgent

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

We started seeing our production service trigger a "SLO fallback" on your status page around 07:58 PST and are also seeing increased partial responses / truncated generations in our request logs. This is affecting our chat endpoint (model: rwd-gpt-large-v1) across US region. Sample from our logs attached (zenyard-gen-log-snippet.txt).

Questions:
- Is this a broader hosted issue or something routing-specific to our account/region?
- Is there any chance user data was impacted or requests retried/duplicated?
- ETA on mitigation and whether you plan to route traffic to a fallback model?

We have an active support rotation standing by — Marcus (ops@zenyard.io) is also copied. Please advise next steps and timeline.

Thanks,
Claire Huang
Product Ops — Zenyard

Attachment: zenyard-gen-log-snippet.txt (text/plain, ~8KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: claire.huang@zenyard.io, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ops@zenyard.io
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 08:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observed SLO fallback + partial responses — urgent

Hi Claire — thanks for the heads up and for the log sample. Apologies for the disruption; we can confirm you hit an elevated tail of partial responses tied to a regional fanout saturation event. High-level:

- What happened (initial): an internal routing mis-accounting caused request fanout to some older model-variant pools, which in turn exhausted prefetched KV cache capacity and produced partial/truncated outputs for some in-flight requests.
- Immediate mitigation (done): we triggered regional spillover to secondary pools and temporarily enabled a controlled fallback model (rwd-gpt-medium-fallback) for long-running sessions to preserve latency SLOs.
- Impact: you may have seen truncated responses and a short window where p50/p95 exceeded normal; we are not seeing indications of data exfiltration or request duplication at this time.

Next steps we are taking this morning:
- Ops note attached with the current timeline and short-term mitigations: zenyard-interim-ops-note.pdf
- Full technical postmortem aimed for delivery within 48 hours; interim findings update in 6–12 hours.
- Offer: can schedule a 30-minute sync today to walk through what we did and the mitigation timeline.

Claire, I’ll stay on this thread. Ben and Marissa are looped for technical follow-ups and scheduling. The incident page is live: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-12-29-zenyard-fanout

Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ops@zenyard.io
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observed SLO fallback + partial responses — urgent

Claire / Kimberly — brief technical note from the runtime team:

On Tue, Dec 29, 2026 at 08:12 AM Claire Huang <claire.huang@zenyard.io> wrote:
> We started seeing our production service trigger a "SLO fallback" on your status page around 07:58 PST and are also seeing increased partial responses / truncated generations in our request logs.

Prelim root cause (short): an off-by-one in our internal fanout accounting triggered incorrect host selection for a subset of heavy session workloads. That mismatch produced high KV cache eviction rates and caused token-stream truncation for requests that hit a hot pool.

What we did (ops):
- Enabled spillover routing to us-west-2 secondary pools (re-routed ~18% of requests for Zenyard during the window).
- Temporarily promoted rwd-gpt-medium-fallback for sessions with >512 tokens to reduce tail latency.
- Increased prefetch capacity in the affected pools to limit immediate re-evictions.

Why we think it did not cause duplication/data-loss: we validated canonical request IDs and KV integrity; nothing indicates duplicate writes or leaked payloads. We will include the hashes and audit in the postmortem.

Open items we’ll include in the postmortem: exact fanout accounting path, timeline of degraded API responses, tokenization accounting for affected sessions, and a mitigation plan (code fix + automated guardrails).

Ben Carter
Principal Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

(Internal note: will coordinate a deeper log export for Zenyard and include request-id slices — @Marissa can you confirm availability for the 3pm sync?)
